aerial.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide architectural concept illustration for an exploratory Chicago urban-planning article. Create an oblique aerial visualization of a hypothetical new neighborhood replacing Soldier Field and its two southern parking facilities along Chicago's lakefront. The developable concept is a slender north-south district of about 47 gross acres, approximately 1100 metres long and 170 metres wide on average, NOT the entire Museum Campus. View from southeast toward northwest, with Chicago's South Loop skyline in the distant background, Lake Michigan and preserved harbor water on the right/east, a major existing roadway along the west. Show a coherent sequence of short walkable blocks, mostly 6–12-story brick, limestone and warm modern apartment buildings with active ground-floor shops, narrow streets, protected bike lanes, planted courtyards and a few small public squares. Preserve a broad green lakefront promenade outside the new district. No new towers or buildings in the harbor, no artificial islands, no retained stadium bowl. This is an aspirational design study, not a real photograph, exact surveyed plan or approved proposal. Style: sophisticated architectural competition visualization, believable Chicago materials and fine-grained streets, soft clear late-afternoon daylight, elegant restrained colors, enough detail to see the urban form, no fantasy towers. Landscape composition 3:2. No text, no labels, no logos, no watermark.

street.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide street-level architectural concept image for an exploratory Chicago lakefront-neighborhood planning article. Primary request: visualize daily life in a hypothetical walkable neighborhood on the former Soldier Field and southern parking sites. Street-level eye-height perspective looking east along a short neighborhood street toward a public lakefront green and a glimpse of Lake Michigan. Six to twelve story apartment buildings, Chicago red-brown brick and limestone, varied narrow storefronts, frequent doors, planted courtyards, generous sidewalks, protected cycle tracks, raised pedestrian crossings, modest vehicle traffic and a public waterfront that remains open. Believable human scale, ordinary residents walking, wheelchair access, people cycling and sitting outside a neighborhood cafe. Visually sophisticated architectural rendering, realistic materials, clear soft morning light, leafy summer trees, warm restrained palette. Enough view up the facades to show the building height. This is an aspirational illustration, not documentary photography or an approved plan. No stadium, no megatowers, no private gated waterfront, no water relocated into the street, no text labels, logos or watermark. Landscape 3:2.

limitations: AI-generated architectural atmosphere studies. Neither image is georeferenced; shorelines and landmarks are stylized. Do not use images to establish boundaries, capacity, views, permissions, cost or property value.
